A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

with multiplier

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. Then there are neighbourhoods and a unique $C^k$ map $\varphi$ solving $F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)=0$. More precisely, on suitable open neighbourhoods $P$ of $(a,\lambda_0)$ and $Q$ of $b$,

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

A **symplectic form** on a smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth two-form $\omega$

2. $(T_pM,\omega_p)$ is a [[def-symplectic-vector-space|symplectic vector

The pair $(M,\omega)$ is a **symplectic manifold**. Thus both closedness and
pointwise nondegeneracy are required. A zero-dimensional manifold with its
zero two-form satisfies the definition.

derivations.claim: At any $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, full row rank of $J(q)$ gives a permutation of coordinates $q=(x,y)$ for which the $m\times m$ block $D_yc(q)$ is invertible. Apply [F2] to the smooth map $c$ for each finite $k\ge1$. The resulting local graphs agree with the unique $C^1$ graph on overlaps, so that graph is $C^k$ locally for every $k$ and hence smooth. Thus locally $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is $y=\psi(x)$; $\phi(x)=(x,\psi(x))$ parametrizes it, and $D\phi$ has rank $d-m$ with image $\ker J$.

Define $G(x)=D\phi(x)^TMD\phi(x)$. For every nonzero $\xi$, $D\phi\,\xi\ne0$ and $\xi^TG(x)\xi=(D\phi\,\xi)^TM(D\phi\,\xi)>0$, so $G$ is invertible. Its entries are smooth, and $G^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(G)/\det G$ is smooth because $\det G>0$. For a cotangent coordinate $\pi\in\mathbb R^{d-m}$, put $p=MD\phi\,G^{-1}\pi$. Then $JM^{-1}p=JD\phi\,G^{-1}\pi=0$ and $D\phi^Tp=G G^{-1}\pi=\pi$. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. Then there are neighbourhoods and a unique $C^k$ map $\varphi$ solving $F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)=0$. More precisely, on suitable open neighbourhoods $P$ of $(a,\lambda_0)$ and $Q$ of $b$,

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be convex and open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at every point. If $M\ge0$ satisfies $\|Df(z)v\|_2\le M\|v\|_2$ for every $z\in U$ and $v\in\mathbb R^m$, then

$$\|f(y)-f(x)\|_2\le M\|y-x\|_2\qquad(x,y\in U).$$

derivations.claim: At a point of the compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, permute coordinates as $q=(x,y)$ so $D_yc$ is an invertible $m\times m$ block. Apply [F2] for each finite regularity order; uniqueness makes these graphs agree locally, so the graph $y=\psi(x)$ is smooth. Write $\phi(x)=(x,\psi(x))$ and $T(x)=D\phi(x)$. Since $J(\phi(x))T(x)=0$ and both kernels have dimension $d-m$, $\operatorname{im}T=\ker J$.

After shrinking to a convex coordinate neighborhood, $B(x)=D_yc(x,\psi(x))$ remains invertible and $\|B(x)^{-1}(D_yc(x,y)-B(x))\|\le\frac12$. Set $R_x(y)=c(x,y)-B(x)(y-\psi(x))$. Then $R_x(\psi(x))=0$ and the derivative of $B(x)^{-1}R_x$ has norm at most $\frac12$. The mean-value inequality [F4] gives $\|B(x)^{-1}R_x(y)\|\le\frac12\|y-\psi(x)\|$. Since $B^{-1}c=(y-\psi)+B^{-1}R_x(y)$, it follows that $\|q-\phi(x)\|=\|y-\psi(x)\|\le 2\|B(x)^{-1}\|\,\|c(q)\|$. Compactness makes the constant uniform on a finite chart cover.

For $\bar q=\phi(x)$, put $G=T^TMT$ and define $\bar p=MTG^{-1}T^Tp$. Positive definiteness of $M$ and injectivity of $T$ make $G$ invertible; its smooth entries and positive determinant give a smooth inverse by $G^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(G)/\det G$. Then $J(\bar q)M^{-1}\bar p=0$ and $T^T(p-\bar p)=0$. Since $\ker T^T$ and $\operatorname{im}J(\bar q)^T$ both have dimension $m$ and the latter is contained in the former, $p-\bar p=J(\bar q)^T\eta$ for a unique $\eta$.

The identity $J(\bar q)M^{-1}(p-\bar p)=A(\bar q)\eta$ and [F1] imply $\|p-\bar p\|\le C\|A(\bar q)^{-1}\|\bigl(\|J(q)M^{-1}p\|+\|J(\bar q)-J(q)\|\,\|M^{-1}p\|\bigr)$. The momentum set is bounded and $J$ is locally Lipschitz, so step 2.1 bounds the right side by $C(\|J(q)M^{-1}p\|+\|c(q)\|)$. Thus $\Pi(q,p)=(\bar q,\bar p)$ has the asserted distance bound and lies in $\mathcal M$. If $(q,p)\in\mathcal M$, then $\bar q=q$ and the formula for $\bar p$ returns $p$, so $\Pi$ is the identity there. By [F3] the coordinate formula is smooth, and it is the identity on the consistent phase set in this neighborhood. Shrink the finitely many neighborhoods so their closures lie in an open regular set; continuity keeps $A^{-1}$ and the required derivatives uniformly bounded there. A finite subcover gives finitely many such local retractions and a uniform constant.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

Under the hypotheses of [[def-regular-holonomic-phase-space-and-dynamics]], let $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. It is a smooth manifold of dimension $d-m$. Choose a local configuration chart $\phi:O\subseteq\mathbb R^{d-m}\to Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and write $T=D\phi$, $G=T^TMT$. The cotangent coordinates $\pi=T^Tp$ identify the part of $\mathcal M$ over this chart locally with $T^*Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$: the unique consistent ambient momentum representing $\pi$ is $p=MTG^{-1}\pi$. In these coordinates the restricted canonical one-form $p^Tdq$ is $\pi^Tdx$, so the restricted two-form is $\omega_{\mathcal M}=\sum_{j=1}^{d-m}dx_j\wedge d\pi_j$. It is closed and nondegenerate, hence is symplectic on the regular phase manifold.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Thus $A(q)$ is invertible; its entries are smooth and $A^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(A)/\det A$, so its inverse and the displayed multiplier are smooth on a neighborhood of the chart.

Extend the formula in [F1] to an open neighborhood of $q_0$ on which $A$ remains invertible and define the ambient vector field $(q,p)\mapsto(M^{-1}p,-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda(q,p))$. Let $C$ be a compact subset of the regular phase manifold whose configuration projection lies in a compact regular chart. For each $(q,p)\in C$, the two scaled RATTLE equations in [[def-regular-classical-rattle-step-map]] have unique local roots in neighborhoods of
$$\lambda_0=\mu_0=\frac12A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr),\qquad v=M^{-1}p.$$
In local phase coordinates the position root depends smoothly on $(h,q,p)$, and the momentum root depends smoothly on $(h,q,p,\lambda)$ when the position multiplier is treated as a parameter near its selected root. The local branches agree on overlaps after shrinking their neighborhoods. A finite cover of $C$ therefore gives a common $h_0(C)>0$ for $|h|<h_0(C)$; the derivatives of each fixed finite order are uniformly bounded on this cover, and the two multiplier Jacobians remain uniformly invertible there. The exact position roots can also be kept in an ambient neighborhood of the compact regular configuration projection where $J$ has full row rank, so their constrained positions remain in $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$. At $h=0$ both Jacobians equal $-A(q)$.

Use the data of [[def-regular-holonomic-phase-space-and-dynamics]]. For a consistent input $(q,p)\in\mathcal M$, put $v=M^{-1}p$ and
$$\lambda_* =\mu_* =\frac12A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
For nonzero signed $h$, form the sequential scaled residual equations
$$F_q(\lambda)=h^{-2}c\!\left(q+hM^{-1}\left(p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\lambda\right)\right)=0,$$
$$F_p(\mu;\lambda)=h^{-1}J(q_1)M^{-1}p_1=0,$$
where $q_1,p_{1/2},p_1$ are given by the updates below. The selected multiplier pair, when it exists uniquely, is the local root branch whose limits as $h\to0$ are $\lambda_*$ and $\mu_*$. This defines a partial exact step map; no root-existence assertion is part of this definition.

For such a selected pair $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb R^m$, define
$$p_{1/2}=p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\lambda,\qquad q_1=q+hM^{-1}p_{1/2},$$
$$p_1=p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(q_1)-hJ(q_1)^T\mu.$$
The position and momentum equations are respectively $c(q_1)=0$ and $J(q_1)M^{-1}p_1=0$. At $h=0$ define the step to be the identity.

Here $\lambda,\mu$ are force-level multipliers: the corresponding constraint impulses are $hJ^T\lambda$ and $hJ^T\mu$. This scaling keeps the limiting multiplier equations nonsingular as $h\to0$. The position equation is SHAKE; the final momentum equation is the RATTLE tangency correction.

Let $C$ be a compact subset of the regular phase manifold whose configuration projection lies in a compact regular chart. For each $(q,p)\in C$, the two scaled RATTLE equations in [[def-regular-classical-rattle-step-map]] have unique local roots in neighborhoods of
$$\lambda_0=\mu_0=\frac12A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr),\qquad v=M^{-1}p.$$
In local phase coordinates the position root depends smoothly on $(h,q,p)$, and the momentum root depends smoothly on $(h,q,p,\lambda)$ when the position multiplier is treated as a parameter near its selected root. The local branches agree on overlaps after shrinking their neighborhoods. A finite cover of $C$ therefore gives a common $h_0(C)>0$ for $|h|<h_0(C)$; the derivatives of each fixed finite order are uniformly bounded on this cover, and the two multiplier Jacobians remain uniformly invertible there. The exact position roots can also be kept in an ambient neighborhood of the compact regular configuration projection where $J$ has full row rank, so their constrained positions remain in $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$. At $h=0$ both Jacobians equal $-A(q)$.

The input state is consistent, $(q,p)\in\mathcal M$. For $h=0$, return $(q,p)$ with status `exact-identity`; this branch returns no multipliers or residual norms. For nonzero $h$, fix a compact phase subset $C\subset\mathcal M$ over a compact regular configuration chart with $(q,p)\in C$ and $0<|h|<h_0(C)$, using branch balls $U_q,U_p$ supplied by [[lem-rattle-scaled-position-and-momentum-branches]]. The admissible inputs also include initial guesses $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_q$, $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_p$, tolerances $\varepsilon_q,\varepsilon_p\ge0$, finite correction budgets $N_q,N_p\in\mathbb N_0$, and terminating exact factorization/solve backends $\mathcal B_q,\mathcal B_p$ for the two chord calls. Each backend accepts a square $m\times m$ Jacobian, returns a singularity report exactly when it is singular, and otherwise returns a retained factor object. For every right-hand side, solving on this object terminates with the exact unique solution for that matrix; factorization and retained-factor solves are separate operations, as in [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]]. All evaluations of $c,J,\nabla V$ and the displayed matrix operations in the updates, residual and exact residual-Jacobian evaluations, arithmetic, Euclidean norm evaluation/comparison, and domain-membership tests are returning primitives; no bound on their internal cost is specified. The multiplier domains $U_q,U_p\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ are open balls within the regular branch neighborhoods. Choose the balls so that $F_q$ is $C^1$ on $U_q$ and, for every $\lambda\in U_q$, the corresponding $F_p$ is $C^1$ on $U_p$ and all evaluations in the updates are defined and the corresponding positions remain in the ambient full-row-rank configuration region of the branch lemma. Inconsistent input, missing branch balls, or maps not defined on these domains are outside the algorithm's admissible inputs. For a nonzero-step success, the routine returns the approximate state, both multipliers, and both scaled residual norms; on failure it returns the residual solver's status, last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm, together with any position-stage values already computed.

1. Form
$$F_q(\lambda)=h^{-2}c\!\left(q+hM^{-1}\left(p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\lambda\right)\right).$$
Run [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]] on $F_q$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_q$, initial value $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_q$, budget $N_q$, and backend $\mathcal B_q$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm; do not continue.

2. For its returned $\widetilde\lambda$, compute $\widetilde p_{1/2}=p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\widetilde\lambda$ and $\widetilde q_1=q+hM^{-1}\widetilde p_{1/2}$. Form
$$F_p(\mu)=h^{-1}J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\left(\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\mu\right).$$
Run the same supplier procedure on $F_p$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_p$, initial value $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_p$, budget $N_p$, and backend $\mathcal B_p$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, actual scaled tangency residual norm, and the successful position-stage values; do not continue.

3. If both calls meet their residual tolerances, set
$$\widetilde p_1=\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\widetilde\mu$$
and return $(\widetilde q_1,\widetilde p_1,\widetilde\lambda,\widetilde\mu)$, the norms $\|F_q(\widetilde\lambda)\|_2$, $\|F_p(\widetilde\mu)\|_2$, and status “residual tolerances met”.

For nonzero $h$, leaving a branch ball returns `invalid-trial`, a singular factorization returns `singular-jacobian`, and exhausting either correction budget returns `iteration-budget-exhausted`; the supplier supplies the last valid iterate and its evaluated residual norm in each case. No undefined-evaluation status is needed because the admissible domains require all evaluations to be defined. A successful output with nonzero residuals need not lie in $\mathcal M$; applying the routine again requires a consistent input, for example one restored by [[lem-regular-holonomic-phase-residuals-control-distance-to-phase-manifold]]. The supplier status `root` means only that its stated residual tolerance was met; it does not certify an exact root or a forward-error bound. No finite budget is claimed to succeed on every admissible input.

Let $G:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be the residual map of an implicit equation, where $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is the admissible set for the unknown vector. An exact solution is a point $z^*\in U$ with $G(z^*)=0$.

The **update residual** at an approximate solution $\widetilde z\in U$ is the vector $G(\widetilde z)$, measured in the same units as $z$. If the original equation was divided by a positive step scale $\sigma$, then the **derivative residual** is $G(\widetilde z)/\sigma$, and the corresponding update residual is $\sigma$ times that derivative residual. A residual norm is not a forward-error bound unless a separate inverse or stability estimate converts it to $\|\widetilde z-z^*\|$.

For a first-order vector field $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ on an open time-state domain $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]), take a time $t$, input $y\in\mathbb R^d$, and step $h>0$ with $(t,y)\in D$. For backward Euler, an endpoint $z$ is admissible only when $(t+h,z)\in D$, and its update residual is

$$G_{\rm BE}(z)=z-y-hf(t+h,z),$$

so the derivative residual is $G_{\rm BE}(z)/h$.

For an $s$-stage implicit Runge–Kutta tableau $(A,b,c)$, a stage vector $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)$ is admissible only when $(t+c_jh,Y_j)\in D$ for every $j$. On that admissible set, its stage update residual has blocks

$$G_i(Y)=Y_i-y-h\sum_{j=1}^s a_{ij}f(t+c_jh,Y_j),\qquad i=1,\ldots,s.$$

The stage derivative residual is $G(Y)/h$. These conventions distinguish an equation residual from the distance to its exact root.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be convex and open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at every point. If $M\ge0$ satisfies $\|Df(z)v\|_2\le M\|v\|_2$ for every $z\in U$ and $v\in\mathbb R^m$, then

$$\|f(y)-f(x)\|_2\le M\|y-x\|_2\qquad(x,y\in U).$$

Fix a compact regular configuration chart from [[def-regular-holonomic-phase-space-and-dynamics]] and a compact momentum set. Use the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2d}$ for phase-state differences. Each point of its consistent phase set has a neighborhood $U_j$ with a smooth retraction $\Pi_j:U_j\to\mathcal M$ such that $\Pi_j$ is the identity on $U_j\cap\mathcal M$ and
$$\|\Pi_j(q,p)-(q,p)\|\le C_j\bigl(\|c(q)\|_2+\|J(q)M^{-1}p\|_2\bigr).$$
A finite number of these neighborhoods cover the compact phase set, so one constant works for all of them. In particular, residuals of sizes $O(h^4)$ and $O(h^3)$ admit a consistent restoration at distance $O(h^3)$, uniformly on the chart.

derivations.claim: For $F_q(\lambda)=h^{-2}c(q_1(\lambda))$, [F2] gives $D_\lambda F_q=-A(q)+o(1)$ uniformly on the branch ball. Shrink it so $\|A(q)^{-1}(D_\lambda F_q+A(q))\|\le\frac12$. Since $F_q(\lambda)=0$ at the exact root $\lambda$, [F5] along the segment to $\widetilde\lambda$ gives $\|G(\widetilde\lambda)-G(\lambda)\|\le\frac12\|\widetilde\lambda-\lambda\|$. In the final momentum formula, the initial half-momentum difference contributes $O(|h|\varepsilon_q)$ by step 2.1; changing the position in the smooth force and constraint Jacobian contributes $O(|h|^3\varepsilon_q)$; changing the final multiplier contributes $O(|h|(\varepsilon_q+\varepsilon_p))$ by step 2.2. The residual definitions give $\|c(\widetilde q_1)\|=|h|^2\varepsilon_q$ and $\|J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\widetilde p_1\|=|h|\varepsilon_p$. Work in the phase coordinates of the Statement and choose a slightly larger compact convex coordinate neighborhood on which the branches and their first derivatives are bounded by [F2]. $$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
